title: What If an Octopus Moved Into Your Kitchen? #shorts

lines.text: An octopus just moved into your kitchen, and he's already raiding your fridge with arm number seven!
He has three hearts, and his blood is blue, because it runs on copper.
Two thirds of his neurons live in his arms, so every arm thinks for itself.
Try to catch him? His only hard part is his beak, so he slides right down the drain.
Moral: never play hide and seek with an octopus.

sources: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/ten-wild-facts-about-octopuses-they-have-three-hearts-big-brains-and-blue-blood-7625828/ (three hearts; copper-based hemocyanin makes blood blue; about two-thirds of neurons are in the arms; arms can act semi-independently)
https://livescience.com/55478-octopus-facts.html (eight arms moving independently; beak is the only hard part of the body; 2016 NZ aquarium octopus escaped its tank via a drainpipe)

facts.hedge: kitchen scenario is a comedic what-if; 'slides down the drain' is the playful version of the documented drainpipe escape
